ma_bob_johnson_boulder_1.blurb: A big, free-standing granite block in the Stone Tower part of Lynn Woods, north of Boston, standing roughly 18 to 20 feet tall. It is the largest of the small cluster of blocks that make up Bob Johnson Crag, and it is the first giant boulder you meet on the walk in. Ten problems cover a wide range, from an easy V0 up to V7, with a trio of V6 lines at the harder end and a couple of friendly V1 and V2 problems to get warm on. The climbing mixes styles, so it suits a mixed group better than a single-grade project day. Bring a good pad, since the height asks for it.

ma_elephant_boulder.blurb: A gray granite block about 13 feet tall, sitting beside the trail to the Summit Boulders in the Weetamoo part of Lynn Woods. It holds ten problems that split into two camps: a few easier lines from V0 to V4, and a short run of very hard arete problems from V8 up to V10 that give the boulder its reputation. It sees very little sun, which makes it a good pick on a hot summer day. The hike in is on the long side for Lynn Woods, so plan it as part of a day among the neighbouring Weetamoo and Patina boulders rather than a quick stop.
ma_elephant_boulder.approach: Leave the main parking on broad Ox Pasture Road, pass the pond on its right, and carry straight on along the dirt road. After crossing a small stream through a green culvert, turn left onto a game trail and climb about 150 feet uphill to the block.

ma_bullet_boulder.blurb: One large block among the Rifle Range Boulders in Dogtown on Cape Ann, close to the compost dump and a short walk from the Dogtown lot. Its ten problems run from V0 up to the V5 range, with a good number at V3 and V5, so there is something for newer boulderers and a few lines to push on. The boulder is reached by a small social trail off the path, and its back side shows up after the first band of brush. A pad or two is worth carrying in. Other blocks of the rifle range cluster, including a V5- problem by a vernal pool, are a few minutes away if you want more variety.

ma_battleship_rock.blurb: A tall, lone boulder on a hilltop in the Thayer Brook Conservation Area of Western Massachusetts. Ten boulder problems wrap around it, almost all between V0 and V3, so it works well for beginners and for climbers who want moderate lines rather than a hard project. A large overhang is visible on the way up, and a rope is fixed on the slab side. Problems carry nautical names such as Lifeboat, Torpedo and Prow Traverse. The walk in is about fifteen minutes on a trail that finishes with an uphill stretch, so it suits a short outing.

ma_rook_and_bishop_area.blurb: A small cluster of boulders at the foot of Rose Ledge in Western Massachusetts, scattered around the Introductory Buttress just off the trail. Ten problems cover mostly V1 to V5, with a couple of harder ones near the top end of the range. The long traverse of the Rook Boulder is the centrepiece, and steeper, angular blocks are stacked above it. The first boulders appear on the left soon after you start up the trail beside a cliff, so the walk is short. It sits in the busiest stretch of the ledge's bouldering, making it a handy first stop.

ma_g_wall_aka_h_face.blurb: A narrow, prow-like face up to about 70 feet tall in the old granite quarries at Quincy, southeast of Boston. It holds ten routes, mostly set up as top-ropes with a few that can also be led on gear. Grades run from easy to moderate, so it suits beginners and instructional days. A chimney on the left side gives the wall its best-known line. Anchors sit well back from the edge, so bring extra cord and a few pieces to extend them. The quarry as a whole is heavily used and can be busy.
